Customs Act 1969: This SRO is issued under the powers granted by Section 19(1) of this Act.
The Act provides the legal framework for the assessment of import duties and the regulation of exemptions for industrial goods.
National Board of Revenue: The Government issues this order in consultation with the National Board of Revenue to provide customs and tax concessions for specific industrial materials.
TABLE-1: This table lists specific machinery and spare parts for which the import duty exceeding a fixed percentage, along with all applicable value added tax and supplementary duty, is exempted.
TABLE-2: This table identifies materials for which the import duty exceeding a specified percentage is waived, subject to compliance with the conditions set out in the order.
TABLE-3: This table specifies materials that are granted full exemption from all applicable import duties and value added taxes.
Manufacturer: Registered textile-related industrial units that are members of recognized industry associations are eligible to import specified goods at concessional or duty-free rates for their own industrial use.
Manufacturers must submit a certificate from their respective association and a legal undertaking regarding the proper use of the imported materials to the customs authorities.
Customs: Customs authorities are responsible for verifying the imported items against association-issued certificates, catalogues, and industrial requirements before allowing clearance under the concessional rates.
They oversee the enforcement of compliance, including audits and the application of penalties for misuse of exempted goods under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act.

Trade Association: Trade associations are responsible for issuing certification letters to certify that their member industrial establishments use imported machinery, spare parts, and equipment in their production processes.
The president of the respective trade association is authorized to recommend customs duty concessions for imported goods based on specific statutory notifications.
Customs Duty: Industrial establishments are eligible to receive recommendations for concessional customs duty rates on imported machinery and raw materials, provided the goods are intended for the establishment's internal manufacturing processes.

Customs Act 1969: This act empowers the customs authority to impose and collect duties and taxes on imported goods.
It provides the legal framework under which customs authorities can penalize parties for failure to comply with the declared conditions of use for imported industrial equipment and components.
Customs Authority: The customs authority is responsible for enforcing the regulatory requirements and conditions associated with the importation of industrial machinery and equipment.
They have the legal power to recover standard duty and tax rates and impose penalties in the event of non-compliance with the established industrial usage terms.
Industrial Equipment and Spare Parts: These goods are subject to specific conditions when imported for purposes such as establishment, replacement, balancing, modernization, or expansion (BMRE) of an industrial unit.
Importers must provide an undertaking that these imported items will be strictly utilized for the designated industrial projects or face potential fiscal and legal consequences.
